original_question: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon, construct a simple polygon whose visibility graph is G.
target_in_paper: Section 4.3, Open Problem 33: the visibility graph reconstruction problem for simple polygons, asking for a simple polygon P whose vertex visibility graph is a given graph G. The needed notion of polygon visibility comes from Section 1, and the paper treats the variant with extra boundary-order information separately in Section 4.4, Open Problem 34. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the correct promise-and-output structure: it assumes that G is already known to be realizable as a visibility graph of a simple polygon, and it asks for constructing a realizing polygon rather than recognizing or characterizing such graphs. That matches the paper's reconstruction problem at a high level. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: It should say explicitly that this is the vertex visibility graph of a simple polygon: vertices of G are to correspond bijectively to vertices of the output polygon. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

It should define visibility precisely: two polygon vertices are adjacent exactly when the straight-line segment joining them lies entirely within the polygon; the paper's definition allows the segment to pass through a reflex vertex or graze along a polygon edge. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To be fully stand-alone, it should specify that the polygon is drawn in the plane and that the output polygon must realize G exactly, not merely satisfy known necessary conditions for being a polygon visibility graph. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

It should make clear that no additional input such as the Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the polygon boundary is provided here; recovering that boundary cycle is posed separately as Open Problem 34. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

It should not add a complexity requirement such as polynomial time, because Open Problem 33 is stated only as a reconstruction task; the surrounding context mentions PSPACE only as the best known upper bound on the problem's complexity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

It should stay scoped to arbitrary simple polygons, not to solved special cases such as spiral polygons or tower polygons mentioned in the surrounding discussion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: Given only a graph G, promised to be the vertex visibility graph of some simple polygon P in the plane, construct a simple polygon P whose vertices are in bijection with V(G) and such that, for every pair of vertices u,v in V(G), uv is an edge of G if and only if the straight-line segment joining the corresponding vertices of P lies entirely within P, with visibility understood as in the paper (in particular, the segment may pass through a reflex vertex or graze a polygon edge), and without assuming any additional input such as the Hamiltonian cycle corresponding to the boundary of P. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft clearly targets reconstruction, not recognition or characterization, because it assumes G is already known to come from a simple polygon and asks for an explicit geometric realization. The nearest official formulation is therefore Section 4.3, Open Problem 33. The nearby context needed to make the question self-contained is the Section 1 definition of a polygon's vertex visibility graph, together with the Section 4.4 separation of the distinct task of finding the boundary Hamiltonian cycle. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
